steps.text: In a mixing bowl, combine the sweet potatoes, sugar, eggs, milk, salt, 1/3 cup butter and vanilla. Mix together and pour into a greased 13x9 inch baking dish.

To prepare the topping, combine in a separate bowl the brown sugar, flour, 1/3 cup melted butter and pecans. Mix together and crumble over sweet potato mixture. Bake uncovered at 350 degrees F (175 degrees C) for 35 to 45 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Sweet Potato Casserole VI
raw_recipe.description: In this casserole, sweet potatoes are mashed with sugar, eggs, milk, butter and vanilla and baked with a crumble topping made with brown sugar and pecans.

review.reviewBody: This is a great recipe! I made it for Thanksgiving, our office Christmas party and will make it for our family Christmas dinner. I only use fresh sweet potatoes as I don't care for canned. Also, I don't like to boil potatoes (loses flavor) so what I do is wash about 4 sweet potatoes (leaving skins on), wrap them in aluminum foil and bake them in the oven at 450 degrees for about an hour or until soft. Let them cool, unwrap foil and then cut in half and the skins easily slip off. If you have the time, this is A LOT easier then peeling and cutting sweet potatoes to boil (don't know about you all, but sometimes trying to cut through a raw sweet potato is pretty difficult!!). Anyway, then I follow the recipe from there. Yum! I always get rave reviews. Thanks again for this great recipe!

Just served this for Thanksgiving dinner and everyone loved it! I followed some of the suggestions here and reduced the sugars by half and broiled a few marshmallows on top at the end. It was delicious and it’s going into the annual rotation. I made this in advance last Sunday, cooking the sweet potatoes by baking them in the oven wrapped in foil. After it had cooled completely I put a lid on the dish and put it in the fridge until Thanksgiving morning. I warmed it in a 350 degree oven for about 20 minutes and then topped it with the marshmallows and put it under the broiler for about 2-3 minutes watching carefully. I loved having it finished in advance! Would recommend.

Made this exactly as described, except added fresh grated nutmeg and some cinnamon to the potatoes for spice. I even scaled it up for 15 servings and it still fit nicely into a black Glad serving pan for easy travel. 
Because some in my in-law household don't like pecans, I took a suggestion from another recipe and substituted corn flakes in the topping for 2/3 of the top of the casserole. Both the pecans and the corn flakes were sweet and crunchy/even a little chewy which was AWESOME, and they stayed that way underneath the marshmallows my husband insisted I put on top to broil at the end.
Such a great, easy recipe.
Suggestion for sweet potatoes: I peel them and cut into pieces if I have time, then steam them over my large pasta pot. They cook in 20 minutes while you're getting everything else together and they are so moist and soft when you mash them because of the steaming. This works leaving them peeled and whole as well, just takes a little more time.

I substituted agave syrup for the sugar, and blended the topping (frozen butter, brown sugar, flour and pecans) before sprinkling over the top. Everybody loved it and at least three people have asked for the recipe. It was better than last year's.

I’ve made sweet potato pie before and it turned out good. Never tried sweet potato casserole until this recipe. Listening to the comments of cutting back the sugar, I did too. I also added 1/2 teaspoon of pumpkin pie spice. This was a big hit, all gone and talked about a lot. I used fresh potatoes, pricked with a fork, baked them 70 mins, when cool, the skins come right off. I used 4 potatoes.

Really good recipe … I made a mistake and put the brown sugar in the casserole itself so for the topping I was out of brown sugar and made my own by adding a couple of teaspoons of molasses and it was fantastic; a mistake turned into rave reviews!

Here's what I did to make this a 5 star recipe that everyone raved about:

- Bake fresh sweet potatoes, wrapped in foil, at 450F for one hour.
- Halved the sugar (used only 1/2 cup)
- Added 1/2 cup maple (not pancake!) syrup
- Used only about 1/2-2/3 of the topping on a 9x13" dish. Using the whole amount lays it on too thick.
Easy recipe! Big hit with the family. Taste more like a dessert! I used fresh potatoes, no canned. Also the flavor of the potatoe taste better if you bake and not boil the potatoes!

This is EVERYONE'S favorite at the Thanksgiving table. Even the kids love this. I don't normally like sweet potatoes (in any form) and this casserole is the only way I will eat them. The only change I made was I cut the sugar to 1/3 cup because it was too sweet for our crew with a whole cup BUT that is just a personal preference.

I've made this many times for many different people and it has always been a big hit at the holiday events. 

There have been times where I used canned sweet potatoes instead of fresh to save time. When I do this I omit the sugar from the potatoe portion of the recipe (the syrup in the can makes it sweet enough) and I strain the potatoes out of their syrup. Nobody could tell I used canned sweet potatoes and it was loved by everyone. 

I cut the topping portion in half (I always had extra left when I made a full batch) and put everything in a round casarole dish and that seems to be a good amount for a family event.

I have never made sweet potatoes for Thanksgiving in my entire life, until this year. My boyfriend wanted some kind of sweet potato side dish, so I pulled up my trusty Allrecipes link and found this one. I *highly* recommend this recipe. The potatoes were awesome and were the hit of the entire dinner! They are so sweet and creamy smooth, it was almost like eating dessert instead of a side dish. I mixed up the potatoes and put them in the slowcooker on low heat while the turkey was roasting, about 6 or 7 hours. When the turkey was done, I topped the potatoes with the brown sugar/pecan topping and put the crock in the oven to finish it off - 350 degrees for about 20 minutes. Every person at the table asked for a little doggy bag to take with them (and I had plenty to give away, since I doubled the recipe). I might cut back on the amount of sugar used next time I make this recipe because it was so sweet.
Pie a good day for what is going what
Nice and simple. I can easily add and take away ingredients without major change to the dish. I like adding 1/4 cup of orange juice.

This is my all time favorite recipe for Thanksgiving. I triple the recipe to fit in a 15x10 casserole. The sweet potato mixture can be made ahead and frozen without the topping. You can also mix the flour, brown sugar and pecans ahead and keep in the fridge, but add the melted butter right before you get ready to put in the oven, otherwise your topping will turn into a brick that's difficult to break apart. Learn from my mistakes!

Also, this sweet potato casserole is good cold. I can eat it like ice cream.
Turned out spectacular. My family loved it will definitely make it again
It’s great! Tastes good for such a simple recipe, I’d add some more seasoning next time around though. I cut down the sugar 1/4 cup based on the reviews and it was just sweet enough!
